claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you, I need to understand a bit about your situation.

**First, tell me about the child or children you're claiming for:**

1. **How old is each child you want to claim Child Benefit for?** Please provide their age or date of birth for each child.

   - If they're **under 16**, that's a good start
   - If they're **between 16-19**, they may still qualify if they're in full-time education or certain training
   - If they're **20 or older**, they would not qualify

Also, it would be helpful to know **the names of the children** so I can track everything clearly.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to find out about claiming Child Benefit. I have one child, Alex, who is 5 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have **one child, Alex, who is 5 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, that's excellent - they would automatically qualify based on age. Now I need to check a few more things to complete the eligibility assessment.

Let me move forward with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 1: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

For context, this rule typically applies to older children (16+), but I need to confirm for your records. Since Alex is 5, the answer would be that Alex is not in paid work, correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 5!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 2: Is Alex NOT receiving any benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

For a 5-year-old, this is typically not applicable, but I need to check - is Alex receiving any such benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 3: Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship?**

Again, for a 5-year-old, this is straightforward - Alex wouldn't be in an apprenticeship. Can you confirm that Alex is not in any type of apprenticeship programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 4: Let me check your residency situation. Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common path)
2. You have **settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have **pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme and are:
   - Working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - Actively seeking work, OR
   - Have sufficient resources to support yourself and family, OR
   - Studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - Are a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside
4. You're a **Crown servant living abroad** (or in certain qualifying countries)

Which of these situations describes your current residency status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes things straightforward. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 5: Are you responsible for Alex?**

Responsibility means at least one of the following:
1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying for food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc.) - at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount, OR
3. **You're paying maintenance** under a court order or agreement for Alex's care

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That confirms you're responsible for Alex. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 6: Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim for him?**

For example, is Alex's other parent or anyone else currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or have they applied to?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 7: Where is Alex currently living?**

- **At home with you** (normal living situation)
- **In hospital**
- **In care** (local authority care)
- **Fostered** (with a foster family)

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is at home with me - just a normal living situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 8 (final question): Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for Alex's accommodation and upkeep entirely yourself (or with support from family/friends), rather than the council funding it?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I pay for everything myself. The council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! I have all the information I need. Let me navigate to the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me confirm your eligibility:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!**

Great news! You meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for **Alex**.

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

**Child:** Alex (age 5)
- ✅ Right age (under 16)
- ✅ Not working full-time
- ✅ Not receiving benefits in their own right
- ✅ Not in any disqualifying apprenticeship

**Your Circumstances:**
- ✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You live with and are responsible for Alex
- ✅ No other claimant has been identified
- ✅ Alex is living at home in a normal situation
- ✅ The council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation

### **What You Need to Do Next:**

1. **Apply for Child Benefit** - You can apply:
   - **Online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
   - **By post** using form CH2

2. **Gather Required Documents:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Proof of Alex's identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate

3. **Important Note - High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you'll need to be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which may affect your tax position (though you can still receive the benefit)

4. **Payment Details:**
   - Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits)

### **Helpful Links:**
- How to claim: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
- Eligibility overview: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
